scripts.radio:
Hamjambo wasikilizaji, and welcome back to Kenyans Are Asking. Today, we need to talk about the people we rely on when life hangs in the balance: our healthcare workers. Over eight thousand five hundred health workers were hired under the Universal Health Coverage program during the height of the pandemic. For years, they served on precarious contracts, keeping our dispensaries and sub-county hospitals running. Then came the big commitment from the national government: every single one would be absorbed on permanent and pensionable terms. It sounded like progress. But today, that promise is unraveling. Across the country, these professionals are working with unpaid salaries, and the transition has ground to a halt. Why? Because the National Treasury has failed to release the allocated funds to the Ministry of Health and county governments. When leaders make public commitments without backing them with actual cash flow, it is ordinary citizens who pay the ultimate price. A clinical officer who cannot pay rent cannot focus in the emergency room, and when they strike, public wards empty out. Treasury and Afya House must stop passing the buck. You cannot claim to build universal healthcare while starving the very people delivering it.

Kwa ufupi: Zaidi ya wahudumu elfu nane na mia tano wa afya wa mpango wa UHC waliyoahidiwa ajira ya kudumu hawajalipwa mishahara kwa sababu Hazina Kuu haijatoa fedha. Ahadi bila bajeti inalemaza hospitali zetu na kuhatarisha maisha ya Wakenya.
scripts.voice_note: Hey everyone, here is what is happening this week on Kenyans Are Asking. Remember those eight thousand five hundred UHC health workers the government promised to absorb on permanent and pensionable terms? Right now, many of them are working without pay, and the transition has stalled completely. The counties say they are waiting on Afya House, and the Ministry is waiting on the National Treasury, which simply hasn’t released the funds. These nurses, lab techs, and clinical officers keep our rural clinics afloat every single day. Making grand pronouncements about healthcare reform is easy, but an unfunded promise is just public relations at the expense of frontline workers and sick patients. Treasury needs to release this money immediately. Share this note with someone who cares about our public health system.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: A state promise of permanent jobs is empty without released Treasury funds. Track the actual budget disbursement, not just the political pledge.
scripts.reels: Over 8,500 UHC health workers were promised permanent and pensionable jobs. Today, they are facing unpaid contracts because the National Treasury hasn’t released the funds. You cannot deliver Universal Health Coverage on empty promises and unpaid labor. When healthcare workers are starved of their wages, public clinics shut down, and ordinary Kenyans suffer. Treasury must disburse the cash now. Healthcare is a right, not a political photo op.
